API URL precedence:

1. `--api-url`
2. `MCPJAM_API_URL`, or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` (the same
server without `/api/v1`)\n3. The server saved with the OAuth login (only when that login is the credential; a login saved before
logins recorded their server counts as MCPJam Cloud, and one whose recorded server is not a usable address is refused with exit `

3`)
4. `https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1`

Every command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads results) d
ecides its server when it starts, before it contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that
is not an `http(s)` URL, or that carries credentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the two vari
ables naming different servers. The error masks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not a URL
. A saved login is only sent to its own server: when it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command exits `3
` before any request. `mcpjam cloud status` uses the same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON report,
sets `ok: false`, includes `credential.valid` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credentials are
informational (`credential.valid: null`) and successful.\n\nSuccessful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Using MCP
Jam Cloud as … · project: … · <apiUrl>`). `--quiet` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` redacts A

PI keys.

## Cloud project scope

Most Cloud commands pick one project:

1. `--project <id-or-name>`
2. An explicit `projec

t` field in `--file` / `--json`
3. `MCPJAM_PROJECT`
4. The nearest valid `.mcpjam/project.json`
5. Automatic; the most recently
updated project you can see\n\nEmpty `--project` or `MCPJAM_PROJECT` is a usage error. `MCPJAM_PROJECT_ID` does **not** select a

Cloud CLI project (it is SDK eval reporting only).

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam cloud login
mcpjam clou
d link # writes .mcpjam/project.json (no secrets)\nmcpjam cloud status # zero-network: credential,

deployment, selector
mcpjam cloud eval list # uses the link
mcpjam cloud link --remove
```

`mcpjam cloud eval`
run-inspection commands (`status`, `cancel`, `judge`, `iterations`, `gate`, `compare`, `trace`, `steps`, `screenshot`, `video`) fo
llow the same rule; `--project` is optional. `mcpjam cloud sessions list` does too; `--all-projects` restores a cross-project list

ing and cannot be combined with `--project`. Hosted `readiness` never reads the project link.

## What `--host` means

`--host

` is not one flag. The meaning depends on the command:

| Where | What it selects |
| - | - |
| `server`, `tools`, `resources`
, `prompts` | An **AI client** (`claude`, `chatgpt`, `cursor`, …). The CLI sends that host's `clientInfo`, capabilities, and proto
col version in `initialize`. |\n| `test --host` | One host **template** to emulate for a local suite run: its handshake, tool visi
bility and model settings. Never the real client. |\n| `compat --host` | Which AI clients to report. Repeatable; default is all. |
\n| `cloud eval --host`, `cloud goals`, `cloud studies` | A **saved project Host** (`<id-or-name>`), the client config an eval or
goal run is stamped with. |\n\n`--host` on a local command is mutually exclusive with `--client-capabilities`. A Cloud `--host` is

mutually exclusive with `--server` / `--environment` when those already supply a closed server set.

## Global flags

These f
lags apply to every command. Cloud credentials `--api-key` / `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud`, not the program root.\n\n

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--timeout <ms>` | `30000` | Request timeout in milliseconds |
| `--rpc` | off
| Include raw JSON-RPC request/response logs in JSON output under `_rpcLogs` |\n| `--quiet` | off | Suppress non-result progress
output on stderr |\n| `--no-telemetry` | off | Disable anonymous telemetry for this invocation |\n| `--format <format>` | `human`

on TTY, `json` when piped | Raw output format (`json` or `human`) |
| `-v, --version` | | Print the CLI version |

## Output fo

rmats

The CLI auto-detects whether stdout is a terminal:

* **Interactive terminal**: defaults to `--format human`. For most
commands this is pretty-printed JSON; `server doctor` and the OAuth conformance commands provide dedicated human-readable summarie
s.\n* **Piped or redirected** (CI, `| jq`, agent invocation): defaults to `--format json`, the full structured result.\n* **Confor
mance in CI**: `protocol conformance`, `protocol conformance-suite`, `oauth conformance`, `oauth conformance-suite`, `apps conform
ance`, and `apps conformance-suite` support `--reporter junit-xml` and `--reporter json-summary`.\n* **Explicit `--format`** alway
s wins over the auto-detected default.\n\n**For agents**: raw JSON is the source of truth. Human format is a lossy presentation la
yer. If you're parsing output programmatically, pass `--quiet --format json`.\n\nJSON-valued flags accept inline JSON, `@path`, or
`-` for stdin. `tools call` also accepts `--tool-args-stdin` as a shorthand for `--tool-args -`. Use files or stdin for large pay

ll --url $URL --access-token $TOKEN \
 --tool-name my_tool --tool-args - --quiet --format json
```

## Connecting to servers

The CLI supports two transport modes, selected by which flags you pass:

* `--url ...` selects HTTP.
* `--command ...` sele
cts stdio.\n* `--transport http|stdio` is optional and acts as an explicit override/validator when you want the CLI to reject mism

atched flags early.

### HTTP (Streamable HTTP / SSE)

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam server doctor --url

https://your-server.com/mcp
```

Add auth when needed:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
# Static bearer token

mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN

# OAuth tokens from a prior login
mcpjam server d

octor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --oauth-access-token $TOKEN

# Custom headers
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-s

erver.com/mcp --header "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

### Stdio (local subprocess)

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mc

pjam server doctor --command node --args server.js --cwd /path/to/project -e API_KEY=[REDACTED]
```

Stdio child processes inhe
rit the parent shell environment by default. Use\n`-e/--env` to add values or override inherited ones for the spawned server.\nStr
uctured debug artifacts only record the explicit env keys you pass through\n`-e/--env`; inherited shell variables are not enumerat

ed.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `oauth ...` and `protocol ...` are HTTP-only command groups. They do
> not accept stdio targets.

## Upd
ate notifications\n\nAfter a successful command, the CLI checks whether a newer version of `@mcpjam/cli` is available and prints a

notice to stderr when one is found:

```
Update available: @mcpjam/cli 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0
Run npm install -g @mcpjam/cli to updat

e
```

The check is non-blocking: version data is fetched in a detached background process and cached locally for 24 hours, so
it never slows down your commands. The notice is written to stderr only and never touches stdout or JSON output, so it is safe for
both interactive terminals and AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) that capture stderr. It is suppressed automatically in CI.\n

To opt out, set one of these environment variables before running any command:

| Variable | Effect |
| - | - |
| `MCPJAM_NO
_UPDATE_CHECK=1` | Disable update checks for `@mcpjam/cli` |\n| `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` | Disable update checks (conventional npm o

pt-out) |
| `CI=true` | Automatically suppressed in CI environments |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0` |
Success / all checks passed |\n| `1` | Command ran but reported a failure (e.g., server unhealthy, conformance failed) |\n| `2` |

Invalid arguments or configuration |
